summary: The bill requires the FAA to update aircraft certification rules to ban bleed air systems in all new turbine and turboprop designs, mandate filters on any remaining systems in newly built planes after seven years, and phase out their use in existing designs according to 25/50/100 percent manufacturing targets at 10/20/30 years after enactment.

scores.thoughts: The bill directs the FAA to issue new regulations phasing out bleed air systems but contains no appropriations, funding mechanisms, or direct spending provisions. Any indirect compliance costs fall on manufacturers rather than expanding federal outlays. Therefore the bill has no bearing on government spending.
No tax provisions, credits, or revenue measures appear in the text. The legislation is silent on taxation.

While improved cabin air quality may have ancillary health benefits for passengers and crew, the bill does not address healthcare coverage, delivery systems, or public/private healthcare policy. It is a narrow aviation safety regulation.
The bill concerns aircraft environmental control systems and has no connection to firearms or gun regulations.
No provisions relate to immigration, border policy, or pathways for entry.
The legislation addresses aircraft design standards and contains nothing related to reproductive health or abortion access.
Although the bill references turbine and turbo-prop aircraft, its scope is limited to FAA certification rules for civil aviation; it does not alter military spending or defense procurement.
The measure targets cabin air quality from oil fumes rather than external emissions or environmental protections. It does not expand or limit environmental regulations.
No welfare, nutrition assistance, or social safety-net programs are mentioned.
The bill does not address schools, education funding, or school choice.
Nothing in the text concerns drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.
The legislation contains no criminal penalties, sentencing reforms, or policing provisions.
No trade agreements, tariffs, or import/export rules are implicated.
The bill neither authorizes new deficit spending nor directs debt-reduction measures.
No provisions address legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
Foreign aid is not mentioned or affected.
The bill has no relation to voting access, election integrity, or electoral procedures.
No data-privacy, surveillance, or technology-regulation content exists.
Although flight-crew health is indirectly implicated, the bill does not alter worker protections, collective bargaining, or union rights.
The legislation does not engage with religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
